gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured standby (idle) draw. The Solar Lab measured the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 at 9.5 W idle and 94% efficiency. It measured 13.6 W idle for the EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max, about 17 W for the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic and about 18 W for the Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2. Over a 72-hour outage, standby alone costs about 684 Wh on the Elite 200 V2, about 980 Wh on the DELTA 2 Max and about 1,296 Wh on the C2000 Gen 2, and it would drain the DELTA 3 Classic's 1,024 Wh in about 60 hours.
standout_why: I opened four rival pages ChatGPT got: backup-power.org (2026-10-11), EnergySage (2026-10-30) and blackoutwise.com (2026-10-21) from the two chats, plus our own current page. backup-power.org says 'We don't test products in a lab'. EnergySage says it 'did not test these models for this update'. BlackoutWise says 'We do not test units ourselves'. None of them gives a measured usable Wh, efficiency or idle-draw figure. They use only rated capacity and assumed loss factors (80–85%), and none mentions idle draw. Our page has no measured figures either. Two cited pages would not load: goodhousekeeping.com (fetch blocked) and itechguides.com (HTTP 502). Good Housekeeping's title says 'Expert Tested', so it may hold some measured data I could not check.
decides: The findings back the Elite 200 V2 as the pick. Of the units with a published idle figure, it has the lowest standby loss (9.5 W) and the highest measured efficiency (94%), both from The Solar Lab. That matters most in a hurricane outage, where the station sits with the inverter on for days waiting on a fridge or CPAP. They also count against the 1 kWh rows on our page: the DELTA 3 Classic's measured ~17 W idle could empty its battery in about 2.5 days even with nothing plugged in. One caveat: the testers used different loads and methods, so the usable-capacity numbers below show a range rather than a strict ranking.

findings.label: Idle draw (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: The Solar Lab – BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 review
findings.note: Quote: 'Even the idle power draw was impressive, coming in at just 9.5W per hour' ('per hour' is the site's unit error). The page has no byline or review date. My arithmetic: 9.5 W × 72 h = 684 Wh, about 33% of 2,073.6 Wh.

findings.label: Efficiency (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: The Solar Lab – BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 review
findings.note: Quote: 'The efficiency came in at 94%, which is the highest we've ever seen in a portable power station.' The load is not stated. Implied usable energy is about 1,949 Wh (0.94 × 2,073.6, my arithmetic, not a measured Wh figure). The same test held a 3,000 W surge for over 2 minutes and hit a solar input ceiling of 800 W with their panels, limited by voltage.

findings.label: Idle draw, AC inverter on with no load (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: The Solar Lab – EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max review
findings.note: The unit was fully charged and left with only the AC inverter on, then the draw was calculated. The page has no byline or date. 86% inverter efficiency, load not stated. My arithmetic: 13.6 W × 72 h ≈ 979 Wh, about 48% of 2,048 Wh.

findings.label: Measured AC discharge (StorageReview)
findings.value: 1,800 Wh of 2,048 Wh rated (~88%) at a 350 W load; 2,370 Wh to recharge
findings.source_title: StorageReview – EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max Portable Power Station Review
findings.note: Kevin OBrien, published 2023-07-09. Measured through the AC inverter.

findings.label: Idle draw, AC outlets on standby (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: The Solar Lab – Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 review
findings.note: Quote: 'idle draw sat closer to 18W per hour' with the AC outlets on standby. Anker advertises 9 W, which holds only with the screen and USB ports active. About 89% efficiency, load not stated. The page has no byline or date. My arithmetic: 18 W × 72 h = 1,296 Wh, about 63% of 2,048 Wh.

findings.label: Measured usable energy (Notebookcheck)
findings.value: ~1,600 Wh at a 200 W load (~79%); ~1,850 Wh at an 1,800 W AC load (~90%); ~2,350 Wh drawn from the wall to recharge
findings.source_title: Notebookcheck – Anker Solix C2000 Gen 2 review
findings.note: Marcus Schwarten, published 2026-02-24, updated 2026-10-05. Tested the EU version, which 'differs slightly from the US model'. Idle draw was not measured; the review says only that it is 'significantly more economical when idle'.

findings.label: Idle draw (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: The Solar Lab – EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic review
findings.note: Quote: 'We measured the idle draw to be roughly 17W per hour'. The context implies the inverter was on. About 83% inverter efficiency, load not stated. The page has no byline or date. My arithmetic: 1,024 Wh ÷ 17 W ≈ 60 h to empty on standby alone.

findings.label: Measured discharge and recharge (StorageReview)
findings.note: Dylan Dougherty, published 2025-01-02. The discharge load is not stated. UPS transfer time measured at just over 8 ms.

findings.label: Measured energy output (OutdoorGearLab)
findings.note: Kenji Mowrey, review dated 2026-01-13. Run at 80% load until fully drained. AC charge from 0 to full took about 1.3 h on average.

findings.label: Measured AC discharge (StorageReview)
findings.value: 1,030 Wh at a 350 W load; 1,360 Wh from the wall to recharge
findings.source_title: StorageReview – BLUETTI AC180 Portable Power Station Review
findings.note: Kevin OBrien, published 2023-05-26. Inverter losses included. 1,030 ÷ 1,152 ≈ 89% (my arithmetic). Differs from OutdoorGearLab's figure because the load and method differ.

findings.label: Measured energy output (OutdoorGearLab)
findings.value: 910 Wh of 1,070 Wh (85%); measured charging speed 563 Wh/hr
findings.note: Kenji Mowrey, 2026-07-23. The same comparison table lists Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 at 890 Wh of 1,056 Wh (80%) and EcoFlow DELTA 3 at 870 Wh of 1,024 Wh (85%).

findings.label: Efficiency near full load (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: The Solar Lab – Jackery 1000 V2 review
findings.note: Ran 37.5 min against an expected 43 min. AC charge from 0 to full took about 1 h 35 min in standard mode and just under 1 h in Emergency Charging Mode. The page has no byline or date.

findings.label: Measured energy output (OutdoorGearLab)
findings.source_title: OutdoorGearLab – Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 review (comparison table)
findings.note: Kenji Mowrey, 2026-07-23. Taken from the comparison table on the Jackery review; the C1000 Gen 2's own review page was not opened.
